text: 🇲🇽⚖️ The US won't extend USMCA to 2042. Mexico's answer: fine — it runs to 2036, and we review it every year. "The Treaty stays in force until 2036. We'll do annual reviews." — Marcelo Ebrard, Economy Secretary — Mañanera, July 2, 2026 At the first-ever trilateral meeting of Mexico, Canada and the US, Washington declined a 16-year extension. Mexico negotiates from strength: over 80% of its exports enter the US duty-free, with some of the lowest effective tariffs of any US partner. Next bilateral round: July 20, Mexico City.

🇲🇽💵 <u>ANALYSTS CUT MEXICO'S 2026 INFLATION FORECAST TO 4.20%</u>

Banxico's survey of 41 private-sector analysts just lowered the year-end inflation forecast to 4.20%, down from 4.35%. The trigger: first-half June consumer prices fell at a pace unseen in over two decades, dragging annual inflation to 3.55% — the lowest since October. Growth held at 1.1%, benchmark rate seen closing the year at 6.50%.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>MEXICO'S 13-PROJECT PUSH FOR TECH SOVEREIGNTY: NATIONAL EV + STATE SUPERCOMPUTER</u>

SECIHTI presented 13 projects to Congress to "consolidate technological independence and knowledge ownership in Mexico." Two flagships: Olinia, a 100% Mexican-engineered electric car headed for mass production in 2027, and Coatlicue, the country's first state-owned supercomputer, built with 10 public universities and research centers.

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>PEMEX REABSORBS 40 SUBSIDIARIES — 2013 REFORM BEING REVERSED</u>

Sheinbaum is folding Pemex's ~40 scattered subsidiaries back into one vertically integrated state company, capping output at 1.8 million barrels a day and targeting financial autonomy by 2027. "Pemex will return to efficient operation, without so many scattered boards." The new petroleum laws "substantially reverse" Peña Nieto's 2013 reform that opened the oil to multinationals competing against the nation's own company.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>13.4 MILLION LIFTED OUT OF POVERTY — AND SOME OUTLETS ARE FURIOUS</u>

INEGI's numbers: 13.4 million Mexicans out of poverty since 2018, from 51.9 million down to 38.5 million — a 25% drop. Sheinbaum on the coverage: "In some media it bothers them that poverty went down in Mexico. Instead of 'how good that poverty fell,' it's not even newspaper material." A gas-station story made the front page. The 13 million didn't.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>T-MEC SECURED TO 2036 — EBRARD SEES INVESTMENT RISING, NOT FLEEING</u>

With the uncertainty cleared, Mexico's economy minister isn't bracing for capital flight — he expects the opposite. "What I foresee is that we'll have an even larger flow of investment than we expected," Ebrard said. Treaty locked to 2036, first annual review July 20, with Mexico pushing to cut US Section 232 tariffs and to build penicillin and semiconductors inside North America.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>MEXICO REJECTS UK TRAVEL ALERT AHEAD OF ENGLAND MATCH</u>

Ahead of Sunday's Mexico–England Round of 16 match, the UK issued a travel alert warning its fans of phone theft and spiked drinks. Sheinbaum's reply: "It's safe to visit the country." Nearly a million fans are expected — Mexico City is adding screens to spread the crowds, not restrict movement.

NPR: Mexico ends a 40-year knockout drought, beats Ecuador to advance in World Cup
July 1, 2026 | 🟢

📰 A rare US-media Mexico story with no cartel angle: NPR covers El Tri's 2-0 win over Ecuador — Mexico's first World Cup knockout victory since 1986 — straight and celebratory.

🇲🇽 Sheinbaum watched with CDMX mayor Clara Brugada at a fan fest in Azcapotzalco; around 1 million people gathered at the Ángel de la Independencia. She called it "a source of pride for all Mexicans."

• Mexico played "with heart, with soul and with pride." — Sheinbaum

BLOOMBERG: US Decides Against Renewing USMCA, Shifting to Rolling Talks
July 1, 2026 | 🔴

📰 Bloomberg casts the switch to annual reviews as a slow-motion threat — "prolonged uncertainty" that could stall Mexico's peso rally and its nearshoring boom.

🔍 The number the framing leans on: 85% of Mexico's US-bound goods currently enter tariff-free — presented as Mexican fragility, not as leverage Mexico holds inside deeply integrated North American supply chains.

• Section 232 tariffs have already cut Mexico's steel exports 36.6% and auto shipments 5.1% year-over-year.
• "Yearly reviews would put a drag on one of the best currency rallies in emerging markets." — BBVA

NBC NEWS: Trump won't renew USMCA, "toppling one of the last pillars of stability in global trade"
July 1, 2026 | 🟡

📰 Trump, who in 2019 called the USMCA "the best and most important trade deal ever made by the USA," now walks from his own deal — and NBC's story quotes not a single Mexican official.

🇲🇽 What NBC left out: Mexico's economy minister Marcelo Ebrard said Mexico already signed a 16-year extension and sees "no difference between Mexico, the US and Canada so big that we cannot resolve it."

• "The primary issue the president's been focused on is our trade deficit."
• "Our trade deficits with both Mexico and Canada shot up during the Biden administration."
